defects: Adds hypothesis h : a ≤ b that is not present in (and not needed by) the gold statement, which holds unconditionally over all a b : ℝ

Reimplements total variation from scratch instead of using eVariationOn, and the reimplementation is mathematically broken: the 'sorted' list has no monotonicity/ordering constraint, so arbitrary back-and-forth repeats of points in [a,b] make the candidate sums unbounded above, which (via Real.sSup's junk value convention for sets not bounded above) forces totalVariation to default to 0 rather than b-a, making the produced theorem false for a < b

The existential Finset P is disconnected from the actual sum (which is computed purely from 'sorted'), so P's membership constraints do not meaningfully restrict the partition used in the sum — a vestigial/confused piece of the definition

Changes the codomain/value from ℝ≥0∞ (eVariationOn, matched against ENNReal.ofReal (b-a)) to a real-valued sSup construction, altering the mathematical structure and edge-case behavior (e.g. non-bounded-above sets) compared to the gold statement
No requirement that 'sorted' be nonempty beyond head?/getLast? matching a and b, and no connection ensuring sorted's points are drawn from P
